item.title: China's GJ-21, world's first operational large armed reconnaissance stealth UAV on amphibious assault ship, boasts three core strengths: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 18:32:00
The airborne unmanned warfare formation attends a military parade in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 3, 2025. China on Wednesday held a grand gathering to commemorate the 80th anniversary of the victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. (Xinhua/Deng Hua) China's GJ-21 reconnaissance and strike stealth drone recently completed its first successful takeoff and landing aboard the Sichuan, the country's first Type 076 amphibious assault ship, marking a breakthrough in the Chinese Navy's ability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms, according to the Xinhua News Agency. The GJ-21 is the Chinese military's first carrier-borne stealth drone integrating reconnaissance and strike capabilities. Its successful takeoff and landing demonstrate the Chinese Navy's capability to launch and recover fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms. The GJ 21 is the world's first large stealth strike and reconnaissance drone capable of operating from amphibious assault ships. This test marks the world's first catapult launch of a large stealth strike and reconnaissance drone from an amphibious assault ship, Chinese military affairs expert Zhang Xuefeng, told the Global Times on Friday. Zhang outlined GJ 21's key strengths. First, it boasts outstanding stealth performance. Adopting a flying wing configuration and an S shaped top mounted air intake, the aircraft eliminates strong radar reflection sources and delivers excellent all aspect stealth capability. Its stealth performance is even superior to that of in service stealth fighters. Suited for striking heavily defended targets, it can serve as a vanguard asset to carry out "door kicking" suppression missions, according to Zhang. Moreover, GJ 21 has a substantial combat radius. The flying wing design boosts subsonic cruise efficiency. Though its airframe is far smaller than the J 35 and J 20, its combat radius is comparable, said Zhang. GJ 21 is also low cost and reusable. Unlike hypersonic missiles, it can be recovered and redeployed multiple times. It can also deploy small, low cost glide guided bombs. Under high tempo operations, it offers greater fire delivery efficiency with better cost control. If GJ 21 is deployed aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship, coordination between the Type 076 and aircraft carrier will markedly enhance the carrier strike group's anti surface and land attack capabilities. Furthermore, it can team up with manned fighters for high risk, complex missions such as suppression of enemy air defenses. Manned fighters can clear an aerial corridor while GJ 21 pushes forward to neutralize hostile ground targets and air defense systems, according to Zhang. The Sichuan, bearing hull number 51, is the first Type 076 amphibious assault ship independently designed, developed and built by China. Launched and named on December 27, 2024, it incorporates a fully automated landing guidance system, a new integrated power system, and electromagnetic catapult and arresting technology. It can carry fixed-wing drones, helicopters and amphibious equipment, according to Xinhua. Since its first sea trial in November 2025, the Sichuan has steadily conducted sea trials as scheduled, successfully completing equipment and system checks and tests of overall operational stability, per Xinhua.

item.title: PLA deploys early warning aircraft, reconnaissance drone, fighter jet and bomber in China's Huangyan Dao patrols
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 16:53:00
A Type 054A frigate featured in video footage released by People's Liberation Army (PLA) Southern Theater Command (STC) Photo: screenshot from video footage released on STC's official WeChat account China Coast Guard (CCG) vessels featured in a video footage released by CCG Photo: screenshot from video footage released on CCG's official WeChat account Elements of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Southern Theater Command (STC), including naval and air units, conducted readiness patrols in the territorial sea and airspace of China's Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas on Friday, according to an official release from the STC. On the same day, the China Coast Guard (CCG) conducted law-enforcement patrols in the territorial sea of China's Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas, according to the CCG. Both the STC and CCG said that this is a necessary countermeasure in response to the Philippines' rights-violation and provocative acts. A video released by the STC showed that KJ-500 early warning aircraft, WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance drone, J-16 fighter jet, JL-10 advanced trainer jet, H-6K bomber armed with YJ-12 supersonic anti-ship missiles, and Type 054A frigate participated in the operation. Huangyan Dao is China's inherent territory. Since October, forces of the STC have strengthened readiness patrols in the territorial sea and airspace of Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas, the STC said in the release. Since October, the CCG has enhanced law-enforcement patrols in the territorial sea of Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas, and regulated ships engaged in illegal rights-violation activities in accordance with laws and regulations. Such patrols are aimed at further enhancing control and management over relevant waters and airspace, and serve as an effective countermeasure to cope with all sorts of rights-violation and provocative acts, the STC stressed. While the CCG noted that such patrols are meant to further strengthen orderly management of relevant waters and resolutely safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests. Forces of the STC will resolutely safeguard China's sovereignty and security and firmly uphold peace and stability in the South China Sea, the STC stressed. The video released by the STC showed Chinese naval aviation forces tracking and monitoring a Philippine C-208 military aircraft. A Chinese Air Force aircraft issued a verbal warning: "Philippine military aircraft C-208, you have intruded into China's airspace over Huangyan Dao. Leave immediately, or we will take measures against you. You will bear full responsibility for all ensuing consequences." Global Times

item.title: Reconnaissance setup boosts carrier situational awareness: Chinese expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 22:06:00
A WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance unmanned aerial vehicle Photo: Screenshot from the military channel of the CCTV News As the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy's Liaoning carrier group continues the training in the western Pacific, Japan's Defense Ministry Joint Staff has claimed it has spotted not only vessel movements but also military aircraft activities, mostly those of reconnaissance planes. Against the backdrop of a US-Japan joint exercise, a Chinese expert said the reconnaissance aircraft may be providing situational awareness and intelligence support for the carrier group, while Japan's sensationalism surrounding these reports is driven more by political convenience than by genuine security concerns. On Thursday, when asked to comment on reports that Japan had released data showing that its Air Self-Defense Force had scrambled 442 times in response to Chinese and Russian military aircraft from April to September this year, an increase of nearly 70 percent from the same period last year, including 285 scrambles in response to Chinese military aircraft and 152 in response to Russian military aircraft, as well as the Japanese defense minister's claim that joint China-Russia patrols were a "show of force" against Japan, Chinese Defense Ministry spokesperson Senior Colonel Zhang Xiaogang said that Japan was using its usual tactics to hype up the so-called security threats in its neighborhood. This only served to confirm Japan's dangerous practice of frequently surveilling and harassing legitimate activities conducted by China and Russia, and exposed Japan's tendency to frighten itself with imagined threats, Zhang Xiaogang said. He urged Japan to stop playing such deceptive tricks and refrain from creating and hyping up tensions. On Wednesday evening, Japan's Defense Ministry Joint Staff claimed that a PLA BZK-005 reconnaissance drone and a Y-9 intelligence-gathering aircraft had passed through the Miyako Strait into the Pacific that day. Later on the same day, a Y-9 patrol aircraft flew from the southwest of the Danjo Islands in the Nagasaki Prefecture toward waters northwest of Okinawa Island. Similar monitoring was reported in the preceding days. On October 19, for instance, the Joint Staff claimed a PLA BZK-005 and a Y-9 flew from the East China Sea through the Miyako Strait into the Pacific, circled over the ocean and returned. The same day, a PLA TB-001 reconnaissance/strike drone flew from the East China Sea through the area between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan island into the Pacific. Reports on the Y-9 have been the most frequent during this period, six days of notices on the aircraft, according to the Joint Staff's website. These alleged sightings of Chinese aerial reconnaissance assets have come since the PLA Navy announced on October 14 that it had dispatched the Liaoning carrier group to conduct training in the western Pacific. The PLA Navy said the deployment was a routine training mission carried out as part of the country's annual plan, aimed at testing and improving combat-oriented training and continuously enhancing the ability to fulfill missions. It complies with relevant international law and practice and does not target any specific country or target. Meanwhile, a large US-Japan exercise was held from October 19 to 29. The large-scale "Keen Sword 27" military exercise involved more than 50,000 personnel from the Japan Self-Defense Forces and US forces, the Kyodo News has reported. Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, said that with the Liaoning's far-sea training and the US-Japan exercise overlapping, the Chinese reconnaissance aircraft may, to some extent, be providing situational awareness and intelligence support for the carrier group. This multi-layered reconnaissance setup reflects the PLA Navy's approach to system-based far-sea training and joint operations, Zhang Junshe told the Global Times. It is building a far-sea comprehensive support and situational awareness system, improving the carrier group's sustained combat capability and information advantage in complex waters far from the base. Complementary reconnaissance platforms also enable three-dimensional, real-time battlefield awareness, improving information acquisition and responsiveness in complex electromagnetic environments and high-intensity confrontations. At the same time, it tests and improves system-based combat effectiveness in realistic conditions, reflecting a combat-oriented training approach, Zhang Junshe said. Separately, a CCTV News report on Sunday commented on Japan's footage of a Chinese WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance drone, shot from below, indicating a significant altitude gap between the filming aircraft and the WZ-7. "The drone's maximum flight altitude is about 19,000 to 20,000 meters. If Japan can only look up to observe, locate and track the aircraft, it means Japanese assets cannot reach that altitude. At its maximum height, the drone's reconnaissance, early warning signal transmission and connectivity can reach a new level. China's air and sea advantages are being rapidly established in the relevant waters," military commentator Du Wenlong was quoted by CCTV as saying. On October 14, Japan said that afternoon, a Y-9 operated between the waters southwest of the Danjo Islands and waters northwest of Okinawa. Additionally, a PLA WZ-7 reconnaissance drone flew over the East China Sea. Zhang Junshe said that Japan's frequent releases on Chinese ships and aircraft amount to making a fuss out of nothing. The primary aim is to justify higher defense budgets, military expansion and remilitarization; the second is to manufacture regional tension and a favorable atmosphere for US-Japan military coordination in the Asia-Pacific.

item.title: Chinese Defense Ministry responds to media report on China's third-generation nuclear submarine's missile test
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 21:04:00
Chinese Ministry of National Defense Spokesperson Zhang Xiaogang When asked to comment on Xinhua News Agency's first disclosure that China's newest-generation nuclear submarine had participated in a strategic missile test launch, a Chinese Defense Ministry spokesperson responded at a Thursday press conference. The question noted that Xinhua published an article on October 17, which disclosed for the first time that the Long March nuclear submarine had advanced to its third generation and successfully organized a submarine-launched strategic missile test. This was the first time there was explicit disclosure by state media that the newest-generation nuclear submarine had participated in such a test, prompting speculation abroad about the Type 096 strategic nuclear submarine. Some analysts noted that the disclosure, which came during the US-Japan "Keen Sword 27" exercise, was clearly targeted, the question claimed. Chinese Defense Ministry spokesperson Zhang Xiaogang said he was not aware of the specific situation mentioned. He added that our land and rivers continue to renew themselves, and the Long March carries on. China's nuclear submarine development has followed a path of self-reliance and independent innovation, reflecting a major country's efforts to forge its own sword. This has provided solid support for responding to a complex external environment and safeguarding national strategic security. Meanwhile, another question noted that a press conference for the 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, also known as Airshow China, to be held in December, was held in mid-month. At the press conference, organizers announced that "multiple types of major combat equipment will make their public debut at the airshow." Netizens are wondering whether new stealth fighters, airborne reconnaissance aircraft or more new unmanned equipment will appear. The question also cited recent media reports suggesting that several KJ-3000 aircraft may have been spotted near an aircraft manufacturing plant, indicating that the aircraft has entered mass production. Zhang said the scale and influence of Airshow China continue to expand, increasingly serving as an important window for showcasing China's achievements in national defense and aerospace development, as well as an international event anticipated by military enthusiasts at home and abroad. He advised the public to follow official sources for authoritative information on the specific content and schedule of this year's airshow. Citing new satellite imagery, US media outlet The War Zone (TWZ) claims on October 22 that four of China's new KJ-3000 airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft, also referred to as the KJ-20, have been seen in a Chinese aircraft production facility. Global Times

item.title: Liaoning carrier group expands operations in western Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 22:28:00
Photo: CCTV China's Liaoning aircraft carrier group is conducting far-seas training in the western Pacific, while Japan has reported sightings of over a dozen Chinese naval vessels in the region, including at least four Type 055 large destroyers. Chinese experts say the formidable lineup highlights the Chinese navy's growing capabilities for long-range operations. On Wednesday, Japan reported Chinese vessel activities in the region, including a Type 055 destroyer, a Type 052D destroyer, a Type 054A frigate and a China Coast Guard vessel. The latest reports bring the total number of Chinese naval and coast guard vessels identified in the region in recent weeks to at least 17. One day earlier, Japan's Defense Ministry Joint Staff said in a release that it had spotted two Chinese naval vessels, a destroyer with hull number 117 and a frigate with hull number 546, west of Kume Island in the Okinawa Prefecture at around 10 am that day. The vessels subsequently sailed southeast between Okinawa's main island and Miyako Island toward the Pacific Ocean. A separate release by Japan on the same day said it had spotted another group of Chinese warships, including a destroyer with hull number 102 and a replenishment ship with hull number 903 heading in the same direction. The latest sightings followed a series of releases by Japan's defense ministry earlier in October concerning Chinese naval movements in the western Pacific. The movements came after the Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy announced on October 14 that a carrier task group led by the Liaoning had set out to the western Pacific for training. The exercises are part of the PLA Navy's annual training plan and are intended to test and improve the troops' combat-oriented training capabilities and their ability to fulfill missions, according to the announcement. The training complies with relevant international law and practices and is not directed at any specific country or target, the navy said. The carrier group's movements have also drawn attention from the Philippines. The Armed Forces of the Philippines' Western Mindanao Command claimed that its maritime units tracked the Liaoning task group passing through waters off the Zamboanga Peninsula on October 22, according to Philippine media outlet INQUIRER.net. The report said the fleet was initially spotted northwest of Talulu Point in Siocon, Zamboanga del Norte, before being seen southwest of Maitum, Sarangani, as it moved southeast toward the Celebes Sea. The passage may mark the second time the Liaoning has transited the central Philippine maritime region, following a similar passage in 2024. Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times that the lineup for this deployment is particularly formidable, describing it as a "high-end configuration" of a carrier battle group. He said aircraft carrier formations are complex, carefully designed systems whose composition varies depending on operational plans and mission requirements. In his view, the Type 055 destroyer is expected to become a central component of China's naval operations in distant waters, particularly in escorting aircraft carrier groups. China has 10 Type 055 destroyers in service - eight from a first batch and two from a second batch - with more expected to enter service, Song said. The Type 055 builds on the technological foundation of the Type 052D destroyer but features larger displacement and enhanced combat and logistical support capabilities, Song said. He described the Type 052D as a mainstay model, with some of its missions potentially being taken over by the Type 055 as the latter becomes more widely deployed. The Type 055's primary role in a carrier battle group is to provide outer-perimeter protection, including area air defense and anti-submarine defense, while it also possesses the capability to strike surface and land targets, Song said. The Type 052D will continue to perform combat and support missions in China's near and distant seas, while the Type 055 could take on a greater role in operations farther from China's shores, potentially including escort missions in the Gulf of Aden, he said. "In a word, China's overall naval combat capabilities, including its ability to operate and provide support in distant seas and airspace, are growing significantly," noted Song. Aircraft carriers remain the principal offensive component of carrier battle groups, with their embarked aircraft capable of establishing air superiority and conducting strikes against maritime and land targets at ranges beyond those covered by the ships themselves, he noted. The types of carrier-based aircraft accompanying the Liaoning on its deployment to the western Pacific have also drawn widespread public attention. Following the Liaoning group's return to its home port in June after more than 40 days of a previous far-seas combat-oriented training, footage was released publicly for the first time showing multiple J-15T carrier-based fighter jets taking off from and landing on the carrier, state broadcaster CCTV News reported. The J-15T is a domestically developed, single-seat, heavy carrier-based fighter designed for catapult-assisted takeoff. Based on the J-15, also known as the Flying Shark, the upgraded model features improvements to its avionics, weapons systems and airframe, with enhanced capabilities for carrier operations and maritime adaptability. According to Song, together with attack submarines, replenishment ships and land-based early-warning aircraft, the carrier and its escort vessels form an integrated combat system. Meanwhile, submarines can help counter underwater threats and strike surface and land targets, while replenishment ships provide fuel, ammunition and other supplies needed for sustained operations. The combination of carrier-based aircraft, large destroyers and supporting vessels enables the Chinese navy to conduct more complex operations across distant seas and airspace, Song said.

item.title: Chinese defense firm introduces 40mm cased telescoped ammunition, already fielded by multiple domestic platforms
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 22:41:00
Type 100 support vehicles are reviewed at China's V-Day military parade on September 3, 2025. Photo: Screenshot from Changan Wangjiang A new Chinese 40mm cased telescoped ammunition round can punch through 130 millimeters of homogeneous steel armor from a kilometer away - firepower that leaves conventional shells far behind - while offering three damage modes: armor-piercing, high-explosive fragmentation and programmable airburst. The round is already being used by multiple domestic weapons platforms, a Chinese state-owned defense company said on Monday, while providing footage showing the Type 100 support vehicles and new-generation airborne combat vehicles that debuted during the 2025 V-Day military parade. The projectile of the telescoped ammunition is enclosed inside the cartridge case, making the entire round a single cylinder. A single shot can punch through 130 millimeters of homogeneous steel armor, and easily deal with field fortifications and low, slow and small (LSS) aerial targets, said Changan Wangjiang, a defense company under the China South Industries Group, in a video released on its official social media account on WeChat on Monday. An ammunition storage box inside a vehicle armed with domestic 40mm cased telescoped rounds Photo: Screenshot from Changan Wangjiang The round uses a disruptive two-stage ignition design: the first ignition separates the projectile structure and drives the projectile into a locked position, letting the cartridge case form a sealed chamber. A second ignition then sends the round flying at meteoric speed, giving the cased telescoped ammunition its formidable striking power. The round also uses a dart-like aerodynamic layout and fin stabilization, achieving accuracy of 0.5 meters by 0.5 meters at one kilometer, making it not only powerful, but precise enough for near-perfect hits. The 40mm round currently has three main damage modes. The round's first damage mode is the armor penetration mode. Able to punch through 130mm of steel plate from a kilometer away, it can seriously damage main battle tanks. Its second mode, high-explosive fragmentation, sends blast waves in all directions upon impact. Just a few rounds can destroy fortifications and bunkers. The third, programmable airburst, detonates the shell midair to form a dense barrage that leaves drones and other low-slow-small aerial targets nowhere to hide. Cased telescoped ammunition is not new, the concept has existed for years. China pursued it for several reasons, Chinese military affairs expert Song Zhongping told the Global Times. First, tanks and armored vehicles have limited internal space, so cased telescoped rounds allow more ammunition to be carried. Second, they hold more propellant, giving greater striking power. They also generate relatively low recoil and have a neat, regular shape that makes transport easier. The 40mm round is already being used with multiple domestically produced weapons, achieving seamless coverage across all terrains and time periods, a development set to begin a new era of smarter, more efficient Chinese equipment, according to Changan Wangjiang. The information about the new round accompanied footage of Type 100 support vehicles and new-generation domestic airborne combat vehicles, both of which debuted at the V-Day military parade held in Beijing on September 3, 2025. The Type 100 support vehicle can collaborate with the Type 100 tank. While the tank's main gun has strong firepower, the tank faces challenges in engaging multiple targets simultaneously. This is when the fire support vehicle comes in, using its higher rate of fire to suppress and eliminate unarmored targets such as foot soldiers operating anti-tank missiles or lightly armored vehicles, an expert told the Global Times in a previous interview. Airborne combat vehicles can be transported across long distances via the air and provide heavily armored mobile support. They act as the airborne edges in the PLA's fast response and deep strike operations. The large-scale fielding of specially improved conventional munitions shows that the PLA's overall ammunition design philosophy is becoming more forward-looking and more efficient, Song added.

item.title: Philippines claims the Liaoning carrier group transited waters off Mindanao; expert says passage shows routine training with growing tactical flexibility
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 18:31:00
The Liaoning aircraft carrier participates in a dual-aircraft-carrier formation drill on October 21, 2024. Photo: VCG The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy Liaoning carrier task group, currently training in relevant waters of the Western Pacific, was spotted passing through waters off Mindanao last week, the Armed Forces of the Philippines' (AFP) Western Mindanao Command (WestMinCom) claimed on Monday, according to Philippine media INQUIRER.net. This is likely the second time the Liaoning has transited the central Philippine maritime region, after a memorable passage in 2024, a Chinese military affairs expert said, adding that the tactical value lies in the route planning, and that this successful maneuver shows the Liaoning 's far-sea training has brought a wider range of sea lanes into its routine scope. In a statement, WestMinCom claimed its Maritime Situational Awareness Center and other maritime units tracked the Liaoning group as it transited the Zamboanga Peninsula region last Thursday, INQUIRER.net said. Military tracking initially spotted the aircraft carrier fleet northwest of Talulu Point in Siocon, Zamboanga del Norte. The fleet was later monitored southwest of Maitum, Sarangani, as it moved southeastward toward the Celebes Sea, INQUIRER.net claimed. Wang Yunfei, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times that this is likely the Liaoning 's second transit through the central Philippine maritime region. The last time was in October 2024, when the carrier group took a route that seems to have left a deep impression on many. This time, Wang said, the carrier group chose a relatively less-used waterway south of the Philippines instead, with its tactical value lying in the route planning. He noted that the move is consistent with international law and practices. The first practical benefit is avoiding typhoons. A typhoon is currently forming in the Western Pacific, and strong winds and huge waves would severely limit carrier aircraft takeoffs, landings and formation sailing, conditions that are less than ideal for normal training. The waters off south-central Philippines, sheltered by Mindanao and the Sulu Archipelago, offer a natural barrier with much more stable conditions. Choosing this route effectively sidesteps the typhoon zone, ensuring the formation can maintain its training rhythm without being forced to interrupt operations due to bad weather. Second, Wang noted that the route allows another approach into the Western Pacific, with a heading relatively close to Guam, the core hub base for US forces on the second island chain, and a key node for force dispatch, logistics and long-range projection. "In the past, Chinese carriers entering the Western Pacific mostly took the Miyako Strait to the north or the Bashi Channel in the middle, which was easier for Japanese and US reconnaissance to track them continuously and predict their course in advance. Going through the southern Philippines amounts to a new entry channel, making it more challenging for the outside world to predict the direction of operations. Once through these waters and heading east, the formation can directly approach the open Western Pacific near Guam for training," Wang said. The expert also said that a carrier group's long voyage is not simply a show of presence. Far-sea maneuvering itself is the most important part of training. A carrier tests not only whether carrier aircraft can take off, but the entire set of capabilities for navigation, formation coordination, replenishment and concealed maneuvering in unfamiliar waters and complex island and reef channels. Narrow straits, underwater currents, dense islands and reefs, as well as complex electromagnetic environments make for excellent natural training grounds. This maneuver was a highly successful tactical move, Wang said. It shows the outside world that Chinese carriers entering the Western Pacific do not have just two or three fixed routes to choose from. The track also sends a clear signal: the Liaoning 's far-sea training is routine and systematic, not a one-off short cruise, he said. Having passed through the central Philippine maritime region in 2024 and again two years later, the navy has brought this far-sea channel into its routine route planning, familiarizing itself with local sea conditions, hydrology and the electromagnetic environment. This reflects the growing maturity of the PLA Navy's ocean-going planning, able to advance and withdraw freely, maneuver flexibly and steadily hone far-sea combat capability across the vast Western Pacific. On October 14, China's Ministry of National Defense announced that the PLA Navy had organized the Liaoning carrier group to conduct training in relevant waters of the Western Pacific that day. It was a routine training mission under the annual plan, aimed at testing and improving combat-oriented training and continuously enhancing the ability to fulfill missions. It complies with relevant international law and practice and does not target any specific country or target.
